o: oxidation of a substrate in which an outside electron acceptor drives the synthesis of energy by a membrane gradient
the set of reactions that build larger molecules from smaller ones at the cost of energy
a route that serves both to break down and to build up cell material
the set of reactions that break larger molecules down and release energy
items.s: Amphibolic pathway: a route that serves both to break down and to build up cell material. The other options describe Anabolism, Catabolism, Respiration.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Immobilised cell?
o: a microbe anchored to a solid support so that it can be reused in a flowing process
a process in which spent broth is steadily replaced so that the population keeps growing at one rate
a stirred and aerated vessel in which microbes are grown in bulk for a product
a selected microbial preparation added deliberately to bring about a desired change in food
items.s: Immobilised cell: a microbe anchored to a solid support so that it can be reused in a flowing process. The other options describe Continuous culture, Starter culture, Fermenter.

items.q: “the lipopolysaccharide of the outer membrane, released when a Gram-negative cell breaks up” is the definition of
o: Endotoxin
Virulence
Parasitism
Commensalism
items.s: Endotoxin is the lipopolysaccharide of the outer membrane, released when a Gram-negative cell breaks up.

items.q: Biogeochemical cycle may be defined as
o: the reduction of atmospheric dinitrogen gas to ammonia by specialised organisms
illness caused by a toxin that was already formed in the food before it was eaten
the movement of an element through living things, soil, water and air by biological and chemical steps
sealing food in a container and heating it so that spoilage organisms and their spores are destroyed
items.s: Biogeochemical cycle: the movement of an element through living things, soil, water and air by biological and chemical steps. The other options describe Nitrogen fixation, Foodborne intoxication, Canning.

items.q: “a poisonous protein released by a living bacterium into its surroundings” is the definition of
o: Exotoxin
Carrier
Adhesin
Virulence
items.s: Exotoxin is a poisonous protein released by a living bacterium into its surroundings.

a microbe anchored to a solid support so that it can be reused in a flowing process
dried microbial biomass grown in bulk and used as a concentrated feed ingredient
the production of antimicrobial substances as secondary metabolites during the late growth of a culture

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Parasitism?

a surface molecule by which a microbe grips the cells of the tissue it colonises
the degree of harm that a given microbe is able to produce
an association in which one partner lives at the expense of the other
items.s: Parasitism: an association in which one partner lives at the expense of the other. The other options describe Virulence, Mutualism, Adhesin.

items.q: In this course, Zone of inhibition refers to
o: the interference in which one agent reduces the effectiveness of another given with it
the combined effect of two agents that is greater than the sum of their separate effects
the clear ring around a treated disc on a seeded plate where growth has been prevented
the enzyme that splits the ring of penicillin-type drugs and so inactivates them
items.s: Zone of inhibition: the clear ring around a treated disc on a seeded plate where growth has been prevented. The other options describe Antagonism, Beta lactamase, Synergism.

the breakdown of dead organic matter by microbes into simpler substances
the change that makes a foodstuff unfit to eat through microbial growth and enzyme action
the oxidation of ammonia to nitrite and then to nitrate by soil organisms
